title: Why Is Yawning So Contagious? (2 in 3 Catch It) 🥱
description:
Why is yawning contagious? Seeing, hearing or even reading about a yawn can trigger your own: in a Duke study 222 of 328 people yawned at a yawning video, and yawns spread fastest between family and friends.

Sources:
https://www.eurekalert.org/pub_releases/2014-03/dumc-cym031114.php
https://www.livescience.com/17365-yawns-contagious-friends.html
https://www.psychologytoday.com/us/blog/the-athletes-way/201403/why-is-yawning-so-contagious

Animated in the Chalkboard Lesson style.
pinned_comment: Be honest: did you yawn while watching this? 🥱
script:
Why can't you stop yourself from catching a yawn?
Even reading the word yawn can set one off.
You might be fighting one right now.
Seeing, hearing, or just thinking about a yawn
can trigger your own.
In one Duke study,
three hundred twenty eight people watched a three minute video of yawns.
Two hundred twenty two of them yawned too.
That's about two out of three!
And who's yawning matters.
An Italian study found yawns spread fastest between family,
then friends,
and slowest between strangers.
So some scientists link it to empathy,
your brain quietly copying the people you care about.
Little kids don't catch yawns until they're about four.
But your dog can catch yours.
So be honest.
Did you yawn while watching this?
key_facts: Contagious yawning happens in response to hearing, seeing or thinking about yawning (Duke Health press release, 2014)
Duke study: 328 volunteers watched a three-minute yawning video; 222 contagiously yawned at least once (EurekAlert, PLOS ONE 2014)
Norscia & Palagi (Univ. of Pisa): contagion is greatest between kin, then friends, then acquaintances and strangers; authors describe an empathic gradient (Live Science 2011)
Most children aren't susceptible to contagious yawning until about age four (2010 UConn study, via Psychology Today)
Dogs can catch yawns from humans (Live Science)
